segments.en: But when one merits the sanctity of Shabbos — which is the aspect of the illumination of the Ratzon drawn from the inclusivity of son and student, which is the aspect of the illumination of da'as that the tzadik of the generation illuminates and saves Yisrael from sins, as explained in the aforementioned discourse — through this one merits to draw the sanctity of Shabbos into the six weekdays, to sanctify, purify, and refine the aspect of the 39 melachos from the contamination of the Serpent. For one merits that the 39 melachos should be in the aspect of Tal Oaroas, etc., as mentioned above. And through this, all the sins that come from there — from the aspect of the 39 melachos, as is known — are nullified and forgiven. For one merits to sanctify the 39 melachos in the aspect of Tal Oaroas — which is the aspect of the illumination of son and student, which is the opposite of sin, as mentioned above. And therefore through the illumination of the Ratzon, as mentioned above, through this "You have borne the iniquity of Your people" etc., as mentioned above.	33

segments.he: וזה בחי' כוונת המילה הנ"ל שהוא לגלות החסדים הסתומים למעלה להמשיכן למטה למקום גילוי החסדים היינו כנ"ל. כי על ידי מצות מילה שעל ידי זה נכללןי באחד על ידי עוצם הכאב של התינוק שעי"זמעצים עיניו מחיזו דהאי עלמא לגמרי שזהו בעצמו בחי' חיתוך והעברת הערלה וכו' כנ"ל. עי"ז ממשיכין ומגלין החסדים למטה שאז עיקר המשכת החסדים בעולם כידוע בכוונות שכל זמן שהחסדים סתומים למעלה אין החסדים נמשכין בעולם רק כשזודין לתקנם עד שימשיכו אותם במקום הגלוי שאז מאירין ומתפשטין בעולם ולכאורה קשה א"כ מדוע נקאאים בשם חסדים כל זין שהם סתומים כי הלא עיקר חסדו ית' הוא כשעושה חסד עם הבראוים שזהו מדת החסד אבל כל זמן שהם סתויים ואינם מתגלים למטה והשפע של החסד אינ מתפשטת עדיין מדוע נקראים בשם חסדים אך ע"פ הנ"ל למובן הדבר היטב. כי מה שהחסדים סתומים ואינם מתפשטים למטה הוא רק מחמת שעדיין לא זכינו לתקן כלים כראוי בשביל קבלת החסדים וע"כ אז אדרבא זהו עצם החסד מה שהחסדים סתומים למעלה ואין נשפע מהם למטה כ"א מעט דמעט כידוע כי זה לטובה גדולה כי מאחר שעדיין אין כלים לקבל זהו חסד גדול שהם סתומים ואין נמשך מהם למטה כ"א מעט מאד כדי שלא יזיק ריבו השפע ח"ו וכנ"ל. וע"כ ע"י מצוות מילה שעי"ז סותם עיניו מחיזו דהאי עלמא שזהו בחי' העברת הערלה ונכלל באחד ואח"כ שב משם בבחי' רצוא ושוב שזהו בחי' קריאת השם להתינוק שהוא בחי' המשכת התורה וכנ"ל שעי"ז מתקנים הכלים לקבל שפע החסד ע"כ ממילא נמשכין ונתגלין החסדים הסתומים מאחר שכבר נעשו כלים לקבל וכנ"ל. כי עיקר תקון הכלים לקבל שפע החסד הוא ע"י הביטול הנ"ל שעי"ז ממשכיןי תורה מהרשמיו של הביטול שעל ידי זה עיקר תיקון הכלים וכנ"ל:
segments.en: But when the wealth and Malchus are elevated to holiness, then it is the aspect of heh, for all the wealth and all the influences return to holiness. And when Malchus is in the aspect of wealth, then it is the aspect of heh. And this is the aspect of the five shekalim given to the Kohen, for through this the wealth returns to holiness through the Kohen the man of chesed, who cuts the dales from the wicked kingdom. And then Malchus is in the aspect of heh, in the aspect of wealth, in the aspect of va-harikosi lachem berachah ad b’li dai [and I will pour out for you a blessing without limit].

segments.he: אות ז
segments.en: And therefore no one was able to erect the Mishkan except Moshe alone, as it is written: "And Moshe erected the Mishkan" (Exodus 40:18) etc., as our Sages of blessed memory said. For the essence of the illumination of the Ratzon shines only through the aspect of Moshe — who is the aspect of the true tzadik and master of the generation, as explained in the aforementioned discourse. And therefore the essence of the completion of the building of the Mishkan — that is, its erection — was impossible except through Moshe. For each person performed some melachah in the Mishkan according to his level, according to what he merited of some aspect of the illumination of the Ratzon. For certainly not everyone merits the aspect of the illumination of the Ratzon equally, as explained in the words of Rabbeinu of blessed memory elsewhere.	34

segments.he: וז"ש בזוה,ק צווחין ככלבים הב לן מזונא הב לן חיי וכו'. כי עיקר התפילה על בני חיי ומזוני וכו'. צריך להיות בשביל התכלית וכנ"ל. וזה שסיים שם ולא שאלין על מזונא דשכינתא וכו' היינו שצריכין לשאול ולהתפלל רק על תקון הנפש שהוא התכלית שהוא עליית השכינה:
segments.en: And this is the aspect of twenty silver (esrim kesef). For the five shekalim given to the Kohen are twenty silver — this being the aspect of the rectification of the holy Malchus, the aspect of chochmah tata’ah that ascends from the wicked kingdom through the Kohen the man of chesed. And then chochmah tata’ah is joined with chochmah ila’ah, from which is the essential sustenance of chochmah tata’ah, as is explained and understood in the aforementioned discourse. And when chochmah tata’ah and chochmah ila’ah are joined together, this is the aspect of twenty silver. For they are two yuds [each yud = ten] — the aspect of asarah asarah ha-kaf [ten ten the kaf], as is known.

segments.he: אות ח
segments.en: And therefore each person performed melachah in the Mishkan according to the share he had in the aspect of the illumination of the Ratzon. For it was impossible to do any melachah in the Mishkan except through the aspect of the illumination of the Ratzon — in the aspect of "everyone whose spirit moved him" etc., as mentioned above. And therefore the complete finishing of the building of the Mishkan was only possible through Moshe, who merited the illumination of the Ratzon in its completeness. For he was the one who illuminated the illumination of the Ratzon for all the work of the Mishkan. For all the illumination of the Ratzon was drawn from him. And therefore Moshe alone was able to erect the Mishkan, as mentioned above. And this is the aspect of "the Mishkan was erected" (Exodus 40:17) [passive voice] — for the essence of the erection of the Mishkan that Moshe erected was only through the aspect of the illumination of the Ratzon, through which the Mishkan was erected by itself, as mentioned above.	35

segments.he: וזשארז"ל חסידים הראשונים הי' שוהין שעה אחת ומתפללין כדי שיכוונו לבם למקום היינו שהי' שוהין שעה קודם התפלה כדי לכוין לבם ודעתם להש"י לבטל עצמן באור הא"ס דכי לכלול תפלתם באחד שזה עיקר שלימות התפילה כנ"ל וז"ש שם בגמ' שהי' שוהין שעה א' קודם התפלה ושעה א' אחר התפלהכי גם אחר התפלה הי' שוהין שעה אחת כדי להמשיך ולקשר היטב אור הרשימו בדעתם ולבם שעי"ז מקררין ומבטלין כל היסורים וממלאין ומשלימין כל החסרונות כי משם כל תקון הכלים לקבל כל ההשפעות טבוות וכנ"ל. וזהו שמקשו שם וכי מאחרש הי' שוהין ט' שעות בתפלתן תורתן מתי נעשית ומלאכתן מתי נעשית ותירצו מתוך שהי' חסדיים תורתן משתמרת ומלאכתן מתברכת היינו כנ"לשמחמת שהי' שוהין שעה קוה,ת שעי"ז זכו לבחי' ביטול הנ"ל שעי"ז עיקר שלימות התפילה כנ"ל. וכן אחר התפלה שהוא שעה אחת כדי להמשיך ולקשר היטב אור הרשימו בלבם שמשם נמשכת כל התורה ומשם תיקון כל הכלים לקבל כל הברכות וכל ההשפעות ע"כ בוודאי היתה תורתן משתמרת כי משם נמשכת כל התורה כנ"ל. ועי"ז היתה מלאכתן מתברכת כי משם נמשל כל ברכת השפע ע"י תקון הכלים שנמשכין משם שזהו בחי' ויברך אתכם כאשר דבר וכו' וכנ"ל. וע"כ הם נקראים חסידים ע"ש החסד כי רק הם יודעים איך להמשיך החסדים ולגלותם למטה מחמת שהם יודעים לתקן הכלים כראוי ע"י הביטול שלהם ברצוא ושוב וכנ"ל:
segments.en:
And this is what Rashi explains regarding the reason for the five shekalim of the redemption of the firstborn: thus was the sale of Yosef, for twenty silver, since he was the firstborn of Rachel etc. For the commandment of the firstborn was given to Bnei Yisrael immediately upon their going out from Egypt. For the essential Exodus from Egypt depended on this: to subjugate the bechor of the Sitra Achra and to bring out from there the holy bechor. For the essential exile of Egypt began through the sale of Yosef, who was the firstborn. And through this they brought, as it were, the holy bechor — who is the aspect of the holy Malchus — into the exile of Egypt. And particularly because they sold him for twenty silver and blemished the wealth, as mentioned.

And therefore through this precisely the matter unfolded and they descended to Egypt, for they gave power to the kingdom of Egypt, the wicked kingdom, through selling to them the holy bechor who is Yosef as mentioned. And therefore it was impossible for them to leave until Hashem struck all the firstborn of Egypt, in order to subjugate the bechor of the Sitra Achra that was drawing sustenance from the holy bechor — from which came their essential power as mentioned.

And therefore when they left, Moshe himself took the bones of Yosef with him. For in this depended the essential redemption: through returning and bringing out the holy bechor — the aspect of Yosef — from the wicked kingdom. And what Yisrael took of the wealth of Egypt and all their riches is all one aspect, for they are all one, and the entire essential redemption depended on this. For the essential redemption comes through subjugating the wicked kingdom, the bechor of the Sitra Achra, and elevating from there the holy Malchus which is the aspect of the holy bechor, the aspect of Yosef. And then one must bring out all the wealth from the Sitra Achra and bring it into holiness, as mentioned.

And as our Sages of blessed memory said: all of Yisrael were occupied with the plunder, and Moshe was occupied with the bones of Yosef. For in truth it is all one. For what Moshe took — the bones of Yosef, the holy bechor returned and brought out from the wicked kingdom — and what Yisrael took — the wealth of Egypt and all their riches — is all one aspect. And the entire essential redemption depended on this. For the essential redemption comes through subjugating the wicked kingdom, the bechor of the Sitra Achra, and elevating from there the holy Malchus which is the aspect of the holy bechor, the aspect of Yosef. And then all the wealth must be brought out from the Sitra Achra into holiness, as mentioned.

And therefore it was then a great commandment to take the plunder of Egypt, and Hashem blessed-be-He warned them greatly about this, as explained in the verse there. For it is the aspect of rectifying the holy Malchus, on which the essential redemption depends, as mentioned. And therefore when they left Egypt they were immediately commanded the commandment of the firstborn — to redeem him with twenty silver, just as was the sale of Yosef through which they descended into the wicked exile of Egypt. Correspondingly, in reverse: at every time when a firstborn is born, and one must ensure that the wicked kingdom should have no sustenance from there, heaven forbid, one must give twenty silver to the Kohen, the man of chesed. And through this one cuts the holy Malchus from them in the aspect of kitzru l’fi chesed as mentioned.

This too is the aspect of what Rabbeinu explains there in the aforementioned matter in another place: that through this the womb of a woman in difficult labour (makshah leileid) is opened, in the aspect of daltei vitni [the doors of my belly]. And this is the aspect of chatcho l’arba [cutting it into four] — see there and understand well. And this is the aspect of bechor peter kol rechem [the firstborn that opens every womb] that one gives to the Kohen the man of chesed. For through chesed is accomplished the aspect of chatcho l’arba, through which the birth takes place. And the essential birth is the first birth, for the essential is the beginning. Understand this well.

aligned_segments.he: אות א
aligned_segments.en: The general principle, in brief, as it pertains to our matter: through the eating of Israel, a yichud [unification] of the Kudsha Brich Hu [the Holy One, Blessed be He] and His Shechintay [Divine Presence], apin b'apin [face to face], is effected — and so on. However, the eating must be from food that has been clarified [nitbarar], for from food that contains admixture, it is possible to sin through such eating. And the clarification of foods comes about through faith [emunah]. For there are difficulties [kushyos] that can be resolved, and so on; and there are difficulties that cannot be resolved or answered until the Future [the Messianic era], and so on — regarding those, one must simply stand firm in faith. And even the difficulties that do have answers, sometimes the pathways of intellect become blocked and one does not know how to answer them, and so on. The remedy for this is the study of the Poskim [halachic decisors], and so on. But the difficulties for which there is no resolution, it is forbidden for a person to dwell on them — he must only strengthen himself in faith. And when one has faith in completeness, he can attain through his eating a yichud of the Kudsha Brich Hu and His Shechinta, and so on; and to complete the faith, and so on. One must first elevate the sparks [nitzotzos] of the letters of speech. And when the letters of speech are clarified, the speech itself turns and gathers the holy sparks from among the klippos [husks of impurity], and so on. And in order to elevate the sparks of the letters of speech, fasting is required, and so on, for through fasting one cleaves to the back of holiness, and so on, for fasting is of the aspect of returning backward — to the beginning of the fast, and so on. Moreover, the essence of all things is the beginning, for all beginnings are difficult, since one is going from one extreme to its opposite, and so on. It follows that the essence of the power of all the days of one's service [of G-d] is nothing other than the beginning — to which we must return, back to day one, when one began to understand, to fast, which was the start of teshuvah [repentance], which was difficult for him, that beginning, going as it did from one extreme to its opposite. And each day one returns backward to receive strength from that beginning, as above. The general principle is that through fasting one cleaves to the back of holiness, and then the Mayim d'Chasadim [Waters of Lovingkindness] are drawn forth to moisten the constriction of the throat, from the aspect of "my throat is parched" , and so on, for then the three ministers of Pharaoh are subdued: the chief cupbearer, the chief baker, and the chief butcher — who correspond to the trachea [kaneh], the esophagus [veshet], and the veins/arteries [veridin] — which are of the aspect of the lust for eating and drinking, and so on; their sustenance comes from Pharaoh, who [in his Hebrew letters] spells הָעֹרֶף [ha-oref — the back of the neck], that is to say: from behind. And his primary nourishment comes from [corrupt] speech, and so on. And when the letters of speech are clarified through fasting, then the face of holiness is revealed, and so on, so as to extract the swallowed from their mouth — of the aspect of "[there is] a time when one man dominates another man to his own harm" , and so on. Then those distant from Hashem draw near to Him, and faith is completed in perfection, and is adorned with adornments that were never before, and so on. And then his eating is exceedingly precious, for through his eating the Kudsha Brich Hu and His Shechinta are unified, as above. (See there all this very carefully.)

aligned_segments.he: ע"פ התורה ויאמר בועז אל רות וכו' בלקוטי א' סי' ס"ה וכו' ע"ש הכל היטב:
aligned_segments.en: All of this is of the aspect of Pesach and the Exodus from Egypt, for Mitzrayim [Egypt] is of the aspect of meitzar ha-garon [the constriction of the throat] — of the aspect of "my throat is parched", as above. For this was the essence of the Egyptian exile: that speech was in exile, as is well known. And because of this the [festival] is called Pesach — for it was then that the Exodus from Egypt occurred, when speech went forth from the exile; and this is the aspect of Pesach — peh sach [a mouth that speaks], as is brought [in the holy writings]. For Pharaoh is the king of Egypt, whose name [in its Hebrew letters] spells הָעֹרֶף [ha-oref — the nape of the neck]; and he had three ministers, as mentioned above — the chief cupbearer, and so on — who correspond to the trachea, the esophagus, and the veins, which are of the aspect of the lust for eating and drinking. For these three — trachea, esophagus, and so on — are adjacent to the organs of speech, namely to the five articulatory places of the mouth [chameshes motzo'os ha-peh]. Therefore when they overpower, they draw speech toward the nape of the neck, which is the aspect of Pharaoh; and then it is the aspect of the exile of Egypt: that speech is in exile in Egypt in the aspect of the constriction of the throat — of the aspect of "my throat is parched" — and one cannot utter any word before Hashem, as above. And this is the aspect of the exile of Egypt that [recurs] in every generation. And for this, fasting is needed, through which one cleaves to the back of holiness, and so on, as above. And this is the aspect of the prohibition of chametz [leavened bread] and the mitzva of eating matzah.

aligned_segments.he: וזה בחי' מיילה שצריך התינוק לסבול צער וכאב גדול בעת שחותכין ממנו הערלה. כי הערלה דחפיא על ברית הואבחי' זוהמת הנחש שמשם נמשכין כל הפגמים הנחאזין בתאות עוה"ז שהם בחי' חיזו דהאי עלמא כי הערלה הוא בחי' עננין דמכסיין על עיינין שהוא בחי' הענן והחשך של תאות עוה"ז והבליו שמתגברין על העיניים שלא יכוונו הראות להסתכל על התכלית רק להסתכל מן הצד ח"ו על הבלי עוה"ז שהם חיזו דהאי עלמא שפילה. וע"כ כשצריכין להעביר הערלה הזאת צריכן לסבול צער וכאב גדול. שהוא בחי' צער וכאב המילה שסובל התינוק. כדי שע"י הצער והכאב הגדול הזה יסתום עיניו בחוזק גדול כנראה בחוש. שעי"ז הוא נכלל בהתכלית ע"י שסתום ועוצם עיניו בחזקה מחיזו דהאי עלמא. שזהו בעצמו בחי' חתיכת וכריתת הערלה שהוא עננין דמכסיין על עייינין שהוא בחי' חיזו וזוהמא דהאי עלמא כנ"ל. וכמבואר בהתורה הנ"ל היין שם היטב:
aligned_segments.en: For the eating of Israel must be in great holiness, such that their eating be of the aspect of food that is clarified — whereby through such eating they merit to unify the Kudsha Brich Hu and His Shechinta, apin b'apin [face to face], as above. But this is not merited except when faith is complete, as above. And in order to merit this, two rectifications are needed, as explained in the abovementioned Torah-teaching: namely, to study the Poskim, in order to open the mind [da'as] so that the pathways of intellect not be blocked, so as to merit understanding — to resolve the difficulties that can be resolved. And also one needs fasting, in order to bring forth speech from exile and elevate the holy sparks. And afterward, speech turns its face and elevates the remaining sparks of holiness, and so on. Then faith is completed in perfection and one is saved from the difficulties that cannot be resolved — for which one needs only to strengthen oneself in faith. (As explained there in the abovementioned Torah-teaching, well.) And then one merits the aforementioned eating of holiness, through which the Kudsha Brich Hu and His Shechinta are unified, in the aspect of apin b'apin as above. And these two aspects are of the aspect of the rectification of da'as [mind/knowledge] and emunah [faith]. For the rectification of the difficulties that can be resolved, through the study of the Poskim, is of the aspect of the rectification of da'as — whereby one merits complete da'as to understand what it is possible to understand, to answer the difficulties that can be resolved. And the rectification of the difficulties that cannot be resolved, through fasting, is of the aspect of the rectification of emunah, for from those difficulties one can be saved only through faith, as above. In truth, however, everything is one, and everything is included in emunah — (as explained in the aforementioned Torah-teaching) — for the essence of the rectification is emunah, as it is stated there in letter beis [the second section], which begins: "And the clarification of foods is through emunah…" For the truth is that Hashem has set a boundary for the intellect, and so on — see there. It might seem somewhat difficult, for he [Rabbainu] opened with one thing and concluded with two things: for he begins speaking only of emunah — that the clarification of foods is through emunah — and then goes on to elucidate two aspects: the rectification of da'as and emunah. For this explains that the difficulties that can be resolved, which one merits through the study of Poskim, are of the aspect of the rectification of da'as. However, in truth, everything is one — for the rectification of da'as and emunah are all one, and the two are interdependent. And the essence is emunah, which is the foundation of everything, as it is written, "All Your commandments are emunah" . Yet it is known that the vitality of emunah comes from da'as, for emunah is of the aspect of malchus [kingship/sovereignty], whose vitality comes from the ohr ha-panim [the illumination of the face], which is da'as, of the aspect of "in the light of the king's face there is life" . For in truth, even though emunah is precisely to believe with faith alone, without any intellect or reason — for that which the intellect grasps is not called emunah, as explained in the abovementioned Torah-teaching — nonetheless, the root and the vitality of emunah is da'as. For certainly we cannot say of an animal, which has no da'as at all, that it has faith; the essence of emunah exists only with the human being, who has da'as. Rather, Hashem graces us and draws upon our soul and our mind an illumination from a supernal intellect of such [elevated] degree, that through this, the power of emunah is drawn into us — for emunah flows in its root from a supernal and very, very elevated intellect, and from there the power is drawn into us to strengthen ourselves in complete faith. And even though a person can merit complete emunah even without great da'as — as we observe among common folk and women who have complete faith, and this is the essence of emunah: to believe simply, as they do — (as Rabbainu [Rebbe Nachman], of blessed memory, said elsewhere) — nonetheless, one who merits the completeness of sacred da'as, his faith is stronger and stronger. And the more a person merits to increase his da'as in holiness, in Torah and divine service, the more he merits to draw down a wondrous illumination into emunah. And through this, his faith is strengthened increasingly at every turn. For the more he knows, the more he understands that he does not yet know at all — and that he must strengthen himself only in complete faith. And also, because he now sees that many difficulties that once troubled his mind regarding Hashem and the tzadikim have now been resolved for him, through the opening of his mind — through this he learns the hidden from the explicit: that the difficulties which remain obscure to him certainly also have answers, only his mind has not yet opened sufficiently to resolve those difficulties as well, or else they are of the category of difficulties that cannot be resolved in this world in any manner whatsoever. And therefore he is strengthened through this in greater faith at every turn. It follows that through da'as, emunah is strengthened — and, all the more so, the reverse: that the more a person strengthens himself in greater faith, the more a great illumination is added to his mind. For the essence is emunah. As is explained in the Torah-teaching "And his hands were [steady as] faith until the setting of the sun" — that through emunah one merits da'as — see there. And therefore da'as and emunah are both one; they are both included under the name "emunah", for the ultimate purpose of da'as is emunah — of the aspect of "the ultimate of knowledge is that we do not know" . And since the ultimate of da'as is "that we do not know," certainly one need only stand firm in emunah. And this is the ultimate of da'as that one attains: that one does not yet know anything at all — yet through all the da'as one has attained, one understands with wondrous contemplation how much one must strengthen oneself in emunah and rely solely on faith, which is the foundation of everything. And through this the difficulty we raised above is well resolved: Rabbainu, of blessed memory, opened with one thing and concluded with two things — for everything is one, as above.

aligned_segments.he: אות ב
aligned_segments.en: And when one merits to complete faith through the abovementioned rectifications — namely, the study of the Poskim and fasting — which are the rectification of da'as and emunah, as above, which are both included in the rectification of emunah as above — then precisely does one merit the eating of holiness, through which one merits to unify the Kudsha Brich Hu and His Shechinta, apin b'apin, as above. For the Kudsha Brich Hu and His Shechinta are the root of da'as and emunah, which are truly one, as is known. And therefore eating is called by the name of emunah, and also by the name of da'as, as it is stated: "Graze on faith [re'ay emunah]" , and it is written, "Eat, O beloved [ichlu rei'im]" [] — two beloved friends [terein re'in], and so on — who are chosam b'soch chosam [a seal within a seal], of the aspect of da'as. And as is explained elsewhere, eating is of the aspect of da'as — for sacred da'as and emunah are all one, as above.

aligned_segments.he: וע"כ מלין את התינוק ביום השמיני אחר שעברו עליו שבעה ימים שהם כנגד ז' ימי בראשית שהם בחי' ז' ימי הבנין שבהם נברא העולם שכולל כל הז' מדות שבהם טוב ורך כי יש ז' מדות בקדושהוכן להיפך כידוע כי את זלע"ז וכו'. וכל התאוות וכל החמדות שהם חיזו דהאי עלמא נמשכין מהז' מדות כידוע שמשם אחיזת הערלה שהוא בחי' עננין דמכסיין על עיינין שהם בחי' ז' גלדי עינא שנמשכין מבחי' שבעה אלה עיני ה' המשוטטין בכל הארץ שעל זה הזהירו אותנו רז"ל לבלי להסתכל מן הצד ח"ו רק לזכור בכל פעם שיש עין רואה כ"ש דע מה למעלה ממך עין רואה וכו'. וע"כ אנו מוזהרים עיניך לנוכח יביטו ועפעפיך יישירו נגדך שיכווין עיניו ועפעפיו להביט לנוכח ביושר על התכלית. וזה עיקר נסיון של האדם הבעל בחירה שבשביל זה בא לעולם. כיכל התורה תלויה בעיניים כ,ש לא תתורו אחרי לבבכם ואחרי עיניכם וכו'. וע"כ התורה מתחלת מבראשיחת שהוא בחי' תלת גוונין דעינא ובית עין. כיכל התורה נמשכת רק מהרשימו הנ"ל של הביטול כנ"ל בהתורה הנ"ל. ורק בשבי לזה בא האדם לעולם הזה שהוא מלא הבים ותאותשהם חיזו דהאי עלמא שהם רוצים לבלבל את הראות וכשהאדם מתגבר עליהם ומצמם את הראות שלא יסתכל עליהם רק מכוין את הראות להסתכל על התכלית עי"ז דייקא רואה את התכלית מה שאין המלאכים יכולין לראות ולהשיג. כי זה תכלית א"א לראותו ולהשיגו כ"א בסתמיו דעיינין דייקא. היינו דייקא כשעוברים בזה העולם העשי' הרחוק מאד מהתכלית בתכלית הריחוק ושם שם כשמתגברין לסתום עיניו כנ"ל ולכוונם אל התכלית שם דייקא יכולין לראותו ולהשיגו בבחי' מרחוק ה' נראה לי מרחוק דייקא. ע"כ בהכרח שיעבור על התינוק ז' ימי ערלה שהם בחי' ז' גלדי עינא וכו' כנ"ל. ומשם דייקאצריך לבטל עצמו אל התכלית שזהו בחי' צער המילה. שעי"ז הצער והכאב סותם עיניו מחיזו דהאי עלמא ומעביר מעצמו עיקר הערלה בשרשה שהוא זוהמת הנחש עננין דמכסיין על עיינין שזהו בעצמו בחי' חתיכת הערלה בגשמיות וכנ"ל:
aligned_segments.en: And in the Egyptian exile, both were in exile — da'as and emunah. As is brought, in Egypt da'as was in exile. And likewise speech was in exile, of the aspect of heaviness of mouth [keved peh] — which is the aspect of the exile of emunah, for the essence of emunah is through speech. (As is explained elsewhere, and as is understood from the abovementioned Torah-teaching.) And therefore Israel could not exit the exile except through the two abovementioned rectifications — namely the study of Poskim and fasting, as above. But in Egypt it was still before the giving of the Torah, and they had not yet merited the abovementioned rectifications. And if they had waited until they repaired those rectifications, they would have remained submerged in the exile, for the klippos had seized hold of them so thoroughly that it would have been impossible to draw those rectifications there. Therefore Hashem did with us a great kindness and a wondrous miracle — He leaped over [pasach v'dilaig] the appointed end, and shone upon us a wondrous illumination that was not in the natural order of things. As is explained in the Kavanahnnos [mystical intentions for Pesach] — from the immensity of the illumination of the Pesach night, all the mochin [intellects/mindstates] shine, and mochin d'gadlus [expanded intellect] comes before mochin d'katnus [contracted intellect], and so on — see there — and through this was the essence of the Redemption, and so on — see there. That is to say: one must always first repair those abovementioned rectifications. And afterward speech turns its face to gather the remaining sparks, through which the sitra achra [the Other Side] is essentially subdued, and so on, as above. But now, at the Exodus from Egypt, Hashem performed a wonder for us and illuminated the face of holiness with a wondrous illumination before they had merited to repair those rectifications, for Hashem Himself was revealed in Egypt — of the aspect of "I will pass through the land of Egypt — I am Hashem; I and not an angel; I and not a seraph; I and…" . This was the aspect of the revelation of the face of holiness that shone then with a wondrous illumination. Through this came the downfall of Egypt, until many of them abandoned their faith and converted, as it is stated, "And also a great mixed multitude went up with them" . And through this came the Redemption. For the Redemption occurred on the first night of Pesach, when on that very night Sarah was taken to the house of Pharaoh — this is an allusion to the splendor and beauty of speech turning its face toward them, and so on, through which came their subjugation. (As all this is explained in the abovementioned Torah-teaching — see there.) And because of this, chametz was forbidden on Pesach — not to be seen, not to be found — and one must eat only matzah. For chametz is of the aspect of difficulties [kushyos] — of the aspect of "when my heart ferments [yischametz]" , which is stated there in connection with the difficulties that weighed on his heart regarding Hashem. And therefore throughout the year, eating is of the aspect of chametz and matzah.

aligned_segments.he: אות ג
aligned_segments.en: This is hinted at in the Mah Nishtanah — "Why is this night different?" — with the statement: "On all other nights we eat chametz and matzah." Now, seemingly it would have been sufficient to mention only that on all other nights we eat chametz — as it says regarding other vegetables: "On all other nights we eat any vegetable." Why did it also mention matzah? Rather, this alludes to the rectification of Israel's eating throughout the year — for our eating is always, throughout the entire year, of the aspect of eating chametz and matzah, for eating comprises the two abovementioned rectifications, which are the rectification of da'as and emunah. That is: to resolve the difficulties that can be resolved — this is the aspect of chametz, of the aspect of leavening the brain [chimmutz ha-moach], of fermenting the brain and the da'as to resolve and answer what it is possible to resolve. And matzah is of the aspect of the rectification of emunah, which flows from a higher and higher supernal intellect as above — so as not to gaze upon the difficulties that cannot be resolved, as above. And therefore on Pesach — since we had not yet merited those rectifications, as above, but only a wondrous illumination was drawn upon us from above, which is the aspect of the shining of the face of holiness that shines then — the rectification of eating is drawn then only from there. And this is the aspect of eating matzah, which is of the aspect of man [manna], as above — as it is stated of it: "for they did not know what it was" — for it is a most supernal and elevated holy eating, beyond intellect, of the aspect of wondrous faith, as above. But chametz is forbidden on Pesach even in the smallest amount — not to be seen, not to be found — for it is forbidden to enter into any difficulty whatsoever, even those that can be resolved, as above. But throughout the year chametz is permitted, for when one merits those rectifications, then chametz is permitted — for then one merits to draw down the rectification of da'as, to resolve the difficulties that can be resolved — which is the aspect of the rectification of eating chametz throughout the year. And therefore eating of holiness is always of the aspect of chametz and matzah combined, for it comprises both abovementioned rectifications, which are the rectification of da'as and emunah. But now on Pesach it is forbidden to leaven the brain with any difficulty, even those that can be resolved — and therefore it is forbidden to eat even a trace of chametz; rather one eats matzah, which on Pesach is drawn from the supernal illumination as above. [Hebrew — Section 4] וּבְגָלוּת מִצְרַיִם הָיוּ שְׁנֵיהֶם בַּגָּלוּת, הַדַּעַת וְהָאֱמוּנָה... אֲבָל עַתָּה בְּפֶסַח אָסוּר לְהַחֲמִיץ הַמֹּחַ בְּשׁוּם קֻשְׁיָא... 5. And therefore, after the seventh day of Pesach — which is the Splitting of the Sea of Reeds [Krias Yam Suf] — chametz was permitted. For the Splitting of the Sea of Reeds was through the staff of Moshe, and the staff of Moshe is Tat [the Aramaic acronym מט"ט] — Metatron — which comprises the shishah sidray Mishnah [six orders of the Mishnah], which are of the aspect of permitted and forbidden, and so on. This is the aspect of the study of the Poskim, through which the sea of wisdom is split and one merits the rectification of da'as — to resolve and answer the difficulties that can be resolved — and then emunah is strengthened within us, as above. And therefore afterward chametz was permitted — for the permitting of chametz throughout the year is through the aspect of the rectification of da'as, through the study of the Poskim, which is the aspect of the Splitting of the Sea of Reeds, as above. And therefore the Splitting of the Sea of Reeds occurred on the sixth day of the Counting of the Omer — corresponding to the six orders of the Mishnah, which are of the aspect of permitted and forbidden, and so on; these are the essence of the rectification drawn through the study of the Poskim, which is the aspect of the Splitting of the Sea of Reeds — through which chametz was permitted afterward, as above.

aligned_segments.he: וזהו בחי' בין המצרים שבוכין אז על החורבן. כי הבכי' הוא בחי' שסותמין עיניטו ומצטערין על שרואין גודל ריחוקינו מהתכלית עד שאפי' כשרוצין להסתכל לשם קשה מאד מחמת שנחרב בי תמקדשינו מחמד עינינו. ונתרחקנו מאבינו שבשמים כ"כ עד שמגודל הצער מורידין דמעות שהםחלקי הראות. (כשרז"ל ושבו העבים וכו' זה הראות שהולך אחר הבכי כמובא בדבריו ז"ל כ"פ). ועי"ז נדחה לחוץ פגם הראות של חיזו דהאי עלמא שעיקר בכייתינו על זה על שנמשכנו בראייתינו אחר הסתכלות על הבלי העוה"ז ועי"ז נתרחקנו כ"כ. ע"כ ע"י זאת הבכי' בעצמה שדוחין הדמעות חלקי הראות לחוץ עי"ז מגרשין מעצמו חיזו דהאי עלמא וזוכין להסתכל ביושר על התכלית. וזהו על אלה אני בוכי' עיני עיני יורחדה מים כי רחק ממני מנחם רחק דייקא. כי עיקר הנמחה מכל הצרות הוא הסתכלות על התכלי. ובעוונותינו שהסתכלנו מן הצד רחק ממני מנחם רחק דייקא כנ"ל. כי התכלית רחק מאד רק ע"י שעוצמין עיניו וכו' כנ"ל. עי"ז יכולין להסתכל לשם אבל בעונותינו הרבים שהסתכלנו מן הצד אנו רחוקים מהנחמה שהוא התכלית וכנ"ל. ועיקר הבכי' על שריפת התורה שנמסרו וכו'. כי עיקר הנחמה ע"י הביטול הנ"ל הוא ע"י התורה שממשיכין משם וכו'. ועי"ז יכולין בכל פעם בנקל לחזור ולהתבטל ולהסתכל על התכלית. כי באמת צריך האדם להסתכל תמיד לשם כמו אבות העולם וכו'. אך רוב בני אדם אין זוכין לזה. ע"כ נתן לנו את התורה שהיא נמשכת מהרשימה וכו'. וע"כ עי"ז כשעוסקין באמת ומשימין עיניו ולבו על התורה, עי"ז יכול לחזור ולהתלהב לבו להסתכל לשם. ועי"ז יחזור וימשיך חידושי תורה משם. וזה עיקר בחי' מעלת המחשבות שחושבין תורה וכו' וכן בכל פעם. אבל ע"י החורבן אבדנו הרבה. וע"כ צריכין לבכות הרבה על זהעד שיחזור וימשיך תורה משם שהוא עיקר הנחמה:
aligned_segments.en: One must also on Pesach subdue the three ministers of Pharaoh mentioned above — the chief cupbearer, the chief baker, and the chief butcher — who correspond to [those organs] as above. And this is merited through the Pesach mitzva [slaughtering the Paschal offering], eating matzah, and drinking the four cups [of wine] — which subdue the three ministers mentioned above. For the mitzva of slaughtering the Pesach-offering subdues the chief butcher; the mitzva of matzah subdues the chief baker; and the drinking of the cups subdues the chief cupbearer.

aligned_segments.he: וזהו קול ברמה נשמע נהי בכי וכו' מנעי קולך מבכי וכו' כי יש תקוה לאחריתך לאחריתך וכו'. כי כשאין יכולין לכוין הראות כנ"ל צריכין להתפלל ולצעוק הרבהוזה תלוי בזה. כי שלימות התפילה ע"י הסתכלות הנ"ל וכן הסתכלות הנ"ל ע"י דיבורי התפילה והתורה. וזהו בחי' עיון תפלה עיון דייקא. וזהו גודל המעלה לעשות מהתורות תפילות. וע"כ היום לעשותם ולא למחר כי במתים חפשי וכו'. כי שם בעוה"ב יתבטל אל התכלית בלי שום עשי' כי בזה העולם צריכין לקשר הרשמיו בכמה קשרים שזהו בחי' כלל המצות מעשיות. ועיקר הוא קשירת התפילין שהם עיקר הרשימו וע"כ הם עיקר הדביקו. וע"כ שבת שהוא מעין עוה,ב אין מניחין בו תפילין. כי אז מתקיימת הרשמיו של הביטול בלי עשי' שהוא קשר התפילין:
aligned_segments.en: And this is the aspect of the custom of the firstborn to fast on the eve of Pesach. For the essence of the Exodus from Egypt — which is to bring speech out from the constriction of the throat and to subdue Pharaoh and his three ministers, and so on — is merited through fasting, through which one cleaves to the back of holiness, and so on, as above. And therefore precisely the firstborn fast, for the essence of the virtue of fasting is because one returns each time to the beginning — to when one first began to understand and to fast. And because of this, precisely through fasting, one cleaves to the back of holiness — which is the aspect of returning each time backward, which is the aspect of all the beginnings of holiness, for the essence is the beginning, and so on. And each time one returns to receive strength from the beginning, and so on. (As all this is explained there in the abovementioned Torah-teaching — see there well.) And therefore precisely the firstborn fast on the eve of Pesach, for the firstborn is the beginning — it is the aspect of first and beginning. And therefore the firstborn were sanctified, for the essence is the beginning — and when the beginning is sanctified, through this the rest of the children and the subsequent offspring that follow him are easily sanctified as well. As is stated in the writings of the Ari [HaArizal], of blessed memory: that all the children who come after him receive from the soul-portion of the firstborn, and so on — see there. It follows that the firstborn is of the aspect of the beginning — which is the aspect of the sanctity of fasting. And therefore the essence of the Exodus from Egypt was through the sanctity of the firstborn. (As is explained there in the Parasha of Bo [Exodus 10–13].) For then Hashem slew the firstborn of Egypt and subdued the firstborn of the sitra achra, and saved the firstborn of Israel, the holy firstborn. And then the firstborn were sanctified, as it is stated there: "Sanctify to Me every firstborn…" . For the essence of the Exodus from Egypt is of the aspect of the sanctity of the beginning, which is the aspect of fasting — through which speech goes out from the exile of Egypt and Pharaoh and his ministers, as above, which is the essence of the Exodus from Egypt. And therefore Pesach — which is the Exodus from Egypt — is truly the essence of the beginning, for it is the start of Israel's drawing close to their Father in Heaven: they began to recognize Him and began to draw near to Him at the time of the Exodus from Egypt on Pesach. And then the firstborn were sanctified, for they too are of the aspect of beginning, as above. And therefore it is customarily the firstborn who fast on the eve of Pesach — for the sanctity of fasting is the aspect of the sanctity of the beginning, as above — through which the essence of the aspect of the Exodus from Egypt [is achieved]: to bring speech out from the constriction of the throat, and so on, as above. And therefore Esav, who despised the birthright, sold the birthright through the lust for eating — precisely, as it is stated: "Let me gulp [hal'iteini na]…" . For the sanctity of the birthright is of the aspect of the sanctity of the beginning, which is merited through the breaking of the lust for eating — precisely, which is the aspect of fasting, which is the aspect of the sanctity of the beginning. And therefore the reverse: Esav, who despised the birthright, sold and despised it through the lust for eating — precisely — as it is stated there: "And he ate and drank… and Esav despised the birthright" . For it was precisely through the lust for eating and drinking that he despised the birthright — which is the aspect of the beginning, whose sanctity comes through fasting, through the breaking of the lust for eating and drinking, as above. And Yaakov our forefather merited the birthright then, for each one merited his portion — for as soon as Yaakov saw the intensity of his [Esav's] lust for eating, and that he said to him: "Let me gulp…", Yaakov immediately said to him: "Sell me today your birthright" — that is to say, as per the above: since you are so submerged in the lust for eating, the birthright does not belong to you — for the sanctity of the birthright is through the aspect of fasting, through breaking the lust for eating, as above. And Esav agreed immediately, and sold and despised the birthright for the sake of the lust for eating. And Yaakov gave him bread and a stew of lentils, and he ate, and so on, and he despised, and so on. For Yaakov gave him all the lust for eating — for Yaakov himself had broken the lust for eating, and gave the lust for eating to Esav, and for himself he took in exchange the birthright, which is merited through the breaking of the lust for eating, which is the aspect of fasting, as above.
aligned_segments.he_nikud: וְזֶהוּ, קוֹל בְּרָמָה נִשְׁמָע נְהִי בְּכִי וְכוּ' מִנְעִי קוֹלֵךְ מִבֶּכִי וְכוּ' כִּי יֵשׁ תִּקְוָה לְאַחֲרִיתֵךְ וְכוּ', כִּי כְּשֶׁאֵין יְכוֹלִין לְכַוֵּן הָרְאוּת כַּנַּ"ל צְרִיכִין לְהִתְפַּלֵּל וְלִצְעֹק הַרְבֵּה וְזֶה תָּלוּי בָּזֶה, כִּי שְׁלֵמוּת הַתְּפִלָּה עַל-יְדֵי הִסְתַּכְּלוּת הַנַּ"ל וְכֵן הִסְתַּכְּלוּת הַנַּ"ל עַל-יְדֵי דִּבּוּרֵי הַתְּפִלָּה וְהַתּוֹרָה. וְזֶהוּ בְּחִינַת עִיּוּן תְּפִלָּה, 'עִיּוּן' דַּיְקָא. וְזֶהוּ גֹּדֶל הַמַּעֲלָה לַעֲשׂוֹת מֵהַתּוֹרוֹת תְּפִלּוֹת. וְעַל-כֵּן הַיּוֹם לַעֲשׂוֹתָם, וְלֹא לְמָחָר, כִּי בַּמֵּתִים חָפְשִׁי וְכוּ', כִּי שָׁם בָּעוֹלָם הַבָּא יִתְבַּטֵּל אֶל הַתַּכְלִית בְּלִי שׁוּם עֲשִׂיָּה, כִּי בְּזֶה הָעוֹלָם צְרִיכִין לְקַשֵּׁר הָרְשִׁימוּ בְּכַמָּה קְשָׁרִים, שֶׁזֶּהוּ בְּחִינַת כְּלַל הַמִּצְוֹת מַעֲשִׂיּוֹת. וְעִקָּר הוּא קְשִׁירַת הַתְּפִלִּין שֶׁהֵם עִקַּר הָרְשִׁימוּ וְעַל-כֵּן הֵם עִקַּר הַדְּבֵקוּת. וְעַל-כֵּן שַׁבָּת שֶׁהִוא מֵעֵין עוֹלָם הַבָּא אֵין מַנִּיחִין בּוֹ תְּפִלִּין, כִּי אָז מִתְקַיֶּמֶת הָרְשִׁימוּ שֶׁל הַבִּטּוּל בְּלִי עֲשִׂיָּה שֶׁהוּא קֶשֶׁר הַתְּפִלִּין:

aligned_segments.he: וזהו בחי' מילה בזמנה דייקא דוחא שבת שאז ביטול כל המלאכות הנמשכין מזוהמת הנחש:
aligned_segments.en: And this is the aspect of the Sefirah [Counting of the Omer] — through which we count the days and weeks and return each time to the beginning. For each time we return to the beginning of the offering of the Omer, which was the essential beginning of Israel's drawing close through is'arusa d'lsata [arousal from below]. For on the first night of Pesach, the start of the drawing close was through the abovementioned supernal illumination — which is the aspect of is'arusa d'le'eila [arousal from above]. But afterward — after the first day — that illumination departs. And then we begin to count the Sefirat Ha'omer, to begin to sanctify and purify ourselves in proper order, from day to day, of the aspect of is'arusa d'lsata (as is brought in the holy books). And throughout all the days of the Counting, we return each time to receive strength from the start of the Counting — which is the offering of the Omer — as we say: "Today is two days of the Omer," "Today is three days of the Omer," and so on, for all of them [are counted in relation to the Omer offering]. It follows that each time we return to the beginning — which is the offering of the Omer — and this is the aspect of the sanctity of fasting: returning each time to the beginning. Through this we now merit to go out from the impurity of Egypt and to rectify speech and to merit complete faith, through the aspect of is'arusa d'lsata. For the essential rectification — to bring speech out from the Egyptian exile, and so on — is merited through returning to the beginning. And this is the aspect of fasting, and this is the aspect of the Sefirah, as above.

aligned_segments.he: וע"כ חסידים הראשונים הי' שוהים שעה אחת קודם התפילה כדי שיכוונו לבם למקום להסתכל על התכלית שעי"ז עיקר שלימות התפילה. ואח"כ שעה אחת להמשיך ולקשר היטב הרשימו שמשם התורה. וע"כ עי"ז באמת תורתן מתברכת ענ" לכי משם עיקר התורה כנ"ל ומלאכתן וכו' כי עי"ז מתבטלין כל המלאכות:
aligned_segments.en: And this is the aspect of the prohibition of chailev and dam — in order to subdue and nullify the two kinds of difficulties mentioned above: the difficulties that can be resolved, but for which sometimes the pathways of intellect become blocked and it is impossible to resolve them — for which the study of Poskim is needed; and the difficulties that cannot be resolved, which require one to stand firm only in emunah, which is completed through fasting, through which speech goes forth from the exile of Egypt, and so on — through which faith is completed, as above. For the prohibition of chailev [suet/forbidden fat] is for the sake of the rectification of da'as — so that the pathways of intellect not be blocked, to resolve the difficulties that can be resolved. For chailev is the fatty substance of the body, through which the essence of the intellect is rectified. For the intellect burns like a lit candle through the fatty substance of the body. (As is brought in the words of Rabbainu, of blessed memory, elsewhere.) And therefore it is forbidden to eat the chailev of an animal [beheimah], so that the chailev of the animal not overpower and block the da'as entirely. For when the chalavin [suets] of the sitra achra overpower, the intellect is completely blocked and one can — G-d forbid — forget Hashem, as it is written: "This is their way: folly is theirs" . And our Sages, of blessed memory, expounded: "They have chailev upon their sides [kislayhem]" , and so on. And this is the aspect of "Their fat [chelbamo] has closed [them in]" — of the aspect of "for he covered his face in his fat" . Face [panim] is the intellect — of the aspect of "a man's wisdom illuminates his face" . And through the overpowering of the chalavin, the intellect is enclosed and covered, until one cannot resolve even the difficulties that can be resolved. And through this one forgets Hashem and distances oneself from Him, G-d forbid, for the essential cause of distancing and forgetting Hashem is through heresy [kefirah] and lack of faith, which flow from the difficulties and the concealment of the knowledge of His divinity that is within every heart — (as understood from the abovementioned Torah-teaching). And therefore the Torah warned us against eating chailev — so that the intellect not be blocked and sealed, G-d forbid — so that we merit to understand, to resolve the difficulties that can be resolved. And the prohibition of dam [blood] is for the sake of the rectification of speech, which is the rectification of emunah, as above. For the rectification of speech is to bring speech forth from the exile of Egypt and Pharaoh and his ministers, and so on, as above. And it is known that in Egypt during the exile there was an overpowering of the bloods [damim], and this was the essence of the Egyptian exile — (as explained in the [kabbalistic] writings) — and this is the aspect of "I passed over you and saw you wallowing in your blood" , and so on. For speech comes from the blood [dam], for the blood is the life-force [nefesh], and the essence of speech comes from the nefesh, as it is written: "And the man became a living soul [nefesh chayah]" , and the Targum renders: "a spirit that speaks [ruach memalela]" (as Rabbainu, of blessed memory, brings in many places). And when the bloods of the sitra achra overpower — G-d forbid — then one cannot speak at all, and one is then of the aspect of "I was dumbstruck in silence" — the word dumiyah being of the language of damim [bloods; cognate: ד-מ-מ / ד-מ]. And therefore it is forbidden to eat blood — in order to subdue the evil bloods from which comes the essential exile of Egypt, the essential exile of speech. And through being careful about chailev and dam, one merits to rectify da'as and to bring speech forth from the Egyptian exile — which is the rectification of emunah, as above. And the essence is the rectification of emunah, as above. And the essential rectification is through fasting. And this too is of the aspect of the prohibition of chailev and dam, for through fasting the chailev and the dam are diminished — as we say after a fast: "May it be Your will that the diminishment of my fat and my blood be accepted before You as though I had offered a sacrifice…" . And therefore, by not eating chailev and dam, this is of the aspect of the sanctity of fasting — for "one limb sustains another limb" (as Rabbainu, of blessed memory, brings elsewhere). And if one were to eat chailev and dam, the chailev and dam within the person would increase. But now, by not eating them, the chailev and dam are diminished — which is the aspect of fasting — through which comes the essential rectification of emunah, as above.

aligned_segments.he: וע"כ אחר המילה קורין שם להתינוק הנימול כי עיקר הנחמה מהצער אחר ששבין מהביטול שאז מתגבר הצער ביותר ואז עיקר הנחמה הוא ע"י התורה ששואבין מהזריחה של הביטול וכו' כנ"ל. וזה בחי' השם שקורין אז להתינוק כי השם הוא בחי' התורה כי אורייתא שמא דקוב"ה ומשם נמשכין כל שמות בני ישראל שכולם כלולים בהתורה כי קוב"ה וישראל ואורייתא כולא חד ע"כ ע"י השם שהוא בחי' התורה מחיין את התינוק מהצער והכאב וכנ"ל. וזה בחי' ואומר לך בדמיך חיי ואומר לך בדמיך חיי ב' פעמים היינו בדמיך שהוא הצער והכאב הגדול שסובל בעת החיתוך שנשפך דמו והתיקון לזה לברוח אל התכלית וזהו בדמיך חיי כי שם מקור החיים כ"ש כי עמך מקור חיים וחזר וכפל ואומר לך בדמיך חיי זה בחי' החיות שממשיכין אחר הביטול שמנחמין ומחיין עצמן ע"י התורה שהוא החיים כ"ש כי הוא חייך וכו' וע"כ כפל בדמיך חיי ב"פ כי הא' מורה לברוח אל התכלית מתוך התגברות הדמים והדינים שמשם גודל הצער וזהו בדמיך חיי. כי שם בהתכלית מקור החיים וכנ"ל. ובדמיך חי הב' מורה להחיות עצמו ע"י התורה אחר ששבין מהביטול שזהו בחי' קריאת השם להתינוק אחר המילה וכנ"ל:
aligned_segments.en: And therefore the essence of the sacrifice is chailev and dam. And the chailev ascends upon the altar and is burned entirely as a pleasing aroma to Hashem, for chailev is the fatty substance — the essence of the intellect. But we do not have the power to clarify the holiness and the kedushah that is in the chailev of an animal — and therefore it is forbidden for us to eat it with a severe prohibition. For anyone who eats chailev will have his intellect completely blocked and the heresies and difficulties will intensify within him, G-d forbid, as above. But upon the altar, precisely the chailev ascends as a pleasing aroma, for the Bais HaMikdash [Holy Temple] is of the aspect of da'as and sechel [intellect] — (as Rabbainu, of blessed memory, said many times). And there, supernal intellect and very elevated da'as shines. And therefore there, chailev ascends in the fire as a pleasing aroma — for precisely through it, the intellect shines with great light to reveal His divinity, may He be blessed. For the burning of chailev on the altar is of the aspect of the light of intellect — like a fire burning through the fatty substance of the body, as above — except that we do not have the power to clarify it; but upon the altar it is transformed entirely into holiness. And there, precisely through it, the light of sacred intellect shines, to resolve and nullify all the difficulties that can be resolved — and through this faith is strengthened, as above. And therefore the chailev atones, for the essence of the blemish of all sins consists of heresies, difficulties, and lack of faith, which sins cause — (as we have written many times). And therefore through the sacrifice — through offering the chailev upon the fire on the altar, through which da'as is opened and emunah strengthened, as above — it atones. And similarly dam atones. For in the Bais HaMikdash, the rectification of emunah was drawn through the blood specifically. For blood is of the aspect of the ultimate tzimtzum [contraction] and din [judgment] — from which come the difficulties that cannot be resolved; and therefore blood is forbidden for eating by a common person [hedyot]. But in the Bais HaMikdash, at the altar, through the sprinkling [zerikah] of the blood of the sacrifice, the holiness concealed and hidden within the blood is also clarified and rises. And through this, precisely, the tzimtzum and din are sweetened, and emunah is revealed through this — precisely — for this is the essence of the rectification and atonement for sins, which are of the aspect of heresies, as above. And therefore chailev is eaten and burned entirely upon the altar; but blood is neither eaten nor burned on the altar — rather, it is sprinkled upon the altar, merely touching it. And similarly, the remnants of the blood are poured at the base [yesod] of the altar — they touch the altar and then go out, and are poured into the Kidron brook and sold for fertilizer, and so on — as our Sages, of blessed memory, stated. For chailev is of the aspect of da'as, from which come the difficulties that can be resolved — only that, because of the hold of the klippos and the sitra achra that cleave to the chailev of an animal, we do not have the power to clarify it through our eating, and on the contrary: the intellect and da'as would be completely blocked and sealed if it were eaten. But upon the altar it is burned in great holiness, and then, precisely through it, da'as shines, as above — through which comes the essential atonement, as above. But blood is neither eaten nor burned on the altar — rather, it is sprinkled upon the altar, touching it merely as a fleeting touch. For blood is of the aspect of the ultimate tzimtzum and din, from which come the difficulties that cannot be resolved. And it is explained in the words of Rabbainu, of blessed memory, in the Torah-teaching "Come to Pharaoh" : that these unanswerable difficulties flow from the aspect of the chalal ha-panui [the vacated space], from which He contracted and vacated His divinity, as it were, and so on — see there. And therefore those difficulties cannot be resolved in any manner until the World to Come. And therefore in the Bais HaMikdash, at the altar, a great rectification was made through the blood — for the blood atones, because in the Bais HaMikdash the intellect that will be revealed in the World to Come shines — which is called "holy" [kodesh]. And therefore there, the holiness concealed even in the ultimate tzimtzum — in the aspect of blood — is revealed and shines. And then emunah shines with great light through the sweetening of the tzimtzum and din of the chalal ha-panui — through knowing that even there, His divinity is concealed — through offering the blood upon the altar in the Bais HaMikdash, where the intellect that will be revealed in the Future shines, as above. And therefore blood is neither eaten nor burned upon the altar — for even though in truth the holiness of His divinity is present even in the vacated space, in great concealment, it is in the ultimate tzimtzum, in minimization, in great concealment and hiddenness. And therefore blood is not entirely eaten upon the altar — rather, it is sprinkled on the altar and touches it with merely a fleeting touch, then flows outside. For the holiness ascends from it through the sprinkling, which is a mere touching of the holy altar — since the holiness in the aspect of the vacated space, which is the ultimate tzimtzum of the aspect of blood, is in the ultimate minimization and great concealment — of the aspect of a mere touching, as above. But chailev is entirely transformed into holiness, as above. And therefore it is entirely eaten and burned upon the altar. But both atone — blood and chailev. And in fact, the atonement depends more on the blood than on the chailev — (as explained in the words of our Sages, of blessed memory) — for the essential rectification and atonement comes through the rectification of emunah, which is more fully rectified through the sprinkling of blood on the altar. For through this it is revealed that even in the vacated space, in the ultimate tzimtzum of the aspect of blood, His divinity is hidden and concealed — only in great contraction, of the aspect of a mere touching; but nonetheless, even there, His divinity is concealed. And through this faith is strengthened — and through this is the essence of atonement, as above. For the essence of the strengthening of emunah must be to strengthen oneself against the heresies that come through the difficulties that cannot be resolved — (as is understood from the words of Rabbainu, of blessed memory) — and this is rectified through the sprinkling of blood on the altar. And therefore the essence of atonement is through the blood of the sacrifice, as above.

aligned_segments.he: אות ד
aligned_segments.en: And this is the aspect of melichah [salting the meat] — that one must salt the meat in order to draw out all the blood. For salt is of the aspect of fasting and sufferings [tanis v'yisurin], which purge a person's sins — as our Sages, of blessed memory, stated: (Talmud Berakhot 5a) "A covenant is mentioned regarding salt, and a covenant is mentioned regarding sufferings: just as salt sweetens meat, so too, sufferings purge a person's sins." And sufferings are the aspect of fasting, which is self-affliction and suffering. And as they brought there, in the adjacent passage, regarding the Land of Israel — which comes through suffering — and they cited the verse: "For as a man chastises his son…" . And there that passage speaks of the matter of fasting, as it is written in that context: "And He afflicted you and made you hungry and fed you the manna… and you shall know today, for as a man chastises his son…" . "He afflicted you and made you hungry" — this is the aspect of the affliction of fasting, wherein one makes oneself hungry. And similarly our Sages, of blessed memory, stated in the Midrash: "He afflicted you and made you hungry" — that they fasted before they ate the manna, to purge the food that was in their intestines. For the manna is of the aspect of the aforementioned eating of holiness, which one merits to unify the Kudsha Brich Hu and His Shechinta, apin b'apin — which one merits only through fasting. And therefore they fasted before eating the manna. And therefore our Sages, of blessed memory, stated: "The Torah was given only to those who eat the manna" — for the essence of the Torah is of the aspect of emunah, as it is written: "All Your commandments are emunah" — and this is merited only through breaking the lust for eating through fasting, until one merits the holy eating that is the aspect of manna, as above. For the one depends on the other: through the completeness of emunah one merits eating that is from clarified food, and so on — (as explained there in the abovementioned Torah-teaching) — namely, eating of holiness. And similarly, the more one breaks the lust for eating through fasting and sanctifies one's eating, the more one merits the completeness of emunah — (as explained there — see there). Let us return to the matter. It follows: fasting is of the aspect of sufferings, which are a covenant of salt. And therefore one must salt the meat in order to expel all the blood — for this is the aspect of fasting and sufferings that purge and expel from a person all the evil bloods from which come all evil desires and all sins, G-d forbid, through which emunah is blemished. For through fasting one subdues the klippos and the desires that suckle from speech, and so on, which are the aspect of the exile of Egypt, and so on — which are the aspect of the overpowering of evil bloods, which was the essence of the Egyptian exile. It follows that fasting subdues and expels from a person the evil bloods — which are the klippos and desires — which are the aspect of a blemish of faith. And this is the aspect of salt, as above. And therefore one must salt the meat — for the subduing of the bloods is through salt, which is of the aspect of the sufferings of fasting, as above. And therefore one must salt in a perforated vessel [kli menukav] — precisely. This alludes to the rectification of fasting: that the essential rectification of fasting is to return to Hashem through it, and to examine one's deeds on the fast day, to open and perforate [l'nakev] the heart of stone. As it is written in Isaiah — and this is the Haftarah of Yom Kippur: "Is this the fast I choose?… Is this not the fast I choose: to loosen the bonds of wickedness…" . For the essence of fasting is to open and loosen the bonds of wickedness — to open and break one's heart and extract from it all the knots of wickedness. And so wrote Rabbainu, of blessed memory, in his rhymes [charuzim] printed in the Introduction: "Pierce the heart of stone and illuminate me from there…" (from the liturgical poem printed in the Introduction to Likutay Moharan) Thus he mentioned the rectification of the heart with the expression of piercing the heart. And upon this alludes the perforated vessel: that one must salt the meat to expel the bloods in a perforated vessel — precisely. But in an unperforated vessel, the salting is of no effect — on the contrary, the meat becomes forbidden. This is an allusion: that fasting and sufferings — which are the aspect of salt as above — avail only when one merits to open and pierce his heart of stone, with intention toward Hashem, in order to return from his wickedness; for then through the fasting one merits to drive out and expel the evil bloods — which are all the desires — and to merit complete faith, which is atonement and rectification for all, as above. Amen and Amen.

aligned_segments.he: וזה בחי' סוד כוונת המילה כי מבואר בכתבי האריז"ל שכוונת המילה הוא להמשיך ולגלות החסדים למטה שלא יהי' סתומים למעלה מהחזה וכו' כ"ש שם ע"ש. והענין כי א"א לגלות החסדים כ"א ע"י בח'י המבאור לעיל בהתורה הנ"ל. שהוא ע"י שסותמין עיניו מחיזו דהאי עלמא לגמרי ומסתכלין בו על התכלית האחרון הנצחי שעי"ז עיקר שלימות התפילה וכו' כנ"ל. כי לכאורה קשהמאחר שבאמת כלמה שהש, יעושהעם האדם הכל הוא לטובתו כשרז"ל שצריך האדם לומר כל מה דעבדי ןמן שמיא לטב עבדין א"כ למה צוונו הש"י להתפלל על הצרה ר"ל הלא כל היסורין והצרות ח"ו הם טובות גדולות באמת לזכותו על ידם לחיים נצחיים. אך באמת בוודאי מה שהש"י עושה להאדם הכל לטובה ואעפ"כ הוא צריך להתפלל ולבקש מהש"י לצאת מהצרה לרווחה כי עיקר בריאת העולם הי' בשביל האדם הבעל בחירה היינו שהש"י ברא את העולם שיהי' הכל נמסר ביד האדם שהאדם דייקא יעשה כלים וצנורות להמשיך שפעו וחסדו ית' למטה ובלא תקוני הכלים הנעשים ע"י האדם אין שפע החסד יכול לירד למטה כי אם ירד החסד קודם תיקוני הלכים יהי' בבחי' ריבוי השמן הגורם כיבוי הנר ואזי החסד נתהפך לדין קשה ח"ו ועיקר תקון הכלים הוא ע"י תרוה ותפילה והעיקר ע"י תפילה וכ,ש וכל שיח השדה טרם יהי' בארץ וכו' כילא המטיר ה' וכו' ואדם אין ופרש"י שאדם אין להתפלל וכו' היינו כנ"ל. וע"כ קודם שמתפלל האדם בוודאי הוא טובה גדולהכל מה שבא על האדם אפילו יסורין ח"ו כי הלכ לטובתו כי לפי מעשיו אין יכול ירד לו שום שפע וחיות כ"א ע"י זה וגם זה בחסד גדול כי אם הי' משפיעין לו רק חסד בלא דין כלל הי' ח"ו בבחי' ריבוי אור משזיק יותר וכנ"ל. ע"כ עיקר התיקון ע"י התפילה ועיקר התפילה הוא בחי' המתקת הדינים שע"י התפילה הוא ממתיק הדינים ומתקן כלים שיוכל לקבל שפע חסדו ית' ואז דייקא יכול לבטל היסורין כי יוכל לקבל חסדו וטובתו יתברך הנצחיית בלא היסורין רק על ידי תיקוני הכלים שתיקן על ידי התפילה וכנ"ל. וע"כ עיקר תיקון התפילה הוא על ידי בחי' הנ"ל על ידי שמסתכלין על התכלית וכוללין כל התפילה בא' ששם כולו טוב וכנ"ל. כי בלא זהאין יכולין להתפלל כלל מחמת ענין הקשיא הנ"ל וכמו שהקשה במ"ר וכי נותנין לשוטה ותינוק מה שמבקשין למשל כשאחד יש לו עניות ח"ו או ייסורי הגוף ח"ו ומתפלל שיתן לו הש"י פרנסה ועשירות ובריאות הגוף וכו'. קשה ענין הנ"ל ואיך שייך להתפלל ואיך ישמע הש"י תפילתו ליתן לו פרנסה ובריאות וכו' הלא כוונת הש"י שנותן לו עניות וכו' הוא לטובתו כדי למרק עוונותיו שהוא טובה נצחיית וגם אולי כוונת הש"י מחמת שיודע שאם הי' לו פרנסה מכ,ש איזה עשירות יקלקל מעשיו ביותר כמ ושרואין בחוש כמה מקלקלים רוב העשירים מעשיהם והעושר שמור להם לרעתו אשר על זה התפלא שלמא המע"ה יש הבל וכו' עושר שמור לבעליו לרעתו וכי יש רעה גדולה מזאת כשנותנין לאדם איזה אלפים מטבעות לשחוק בהם בזה העולם הועבר כהרף עין ואח"כ הממון הורגת אותו ועוקרת אותו משני עולמות ח"ו וכ"ש בזו"ק חייכת בהון בעותרא בהאי עלמא ולבתר קטילת להון ר"ל. ע"כ עיקר תקון התפילה הוא ע"י הבחי' הנ"ל שצרייכן מקודם להכלל באחד ולהסתכל רק על התכלית ולידע ולהאמין שהכל לטובה. ואז דייקא יכולין להתפלל אח"כ על כל מה שצריך כי אז יכול להמשיך תיקונים מאור הרשמיו של הביטול שעי"ז יהי' נעשים כלים להמשיך בתוכם רוב שפעו וחסדו שעי"ז יכול לקבל פרנסה ועשירות ובריאות ובני חיי ומזוני וכו' והכל יהי' לטובה מאחר שכבר תיקן כלים כראוי לקבל בהם שפע החסד וזהו בעצמו הענין המבואר בהתו' הנ"ל שאח"כ כששביןמהביטול מכבין צמאון הנפש מהיסורין ע"י התורה שמקבלין מהרשמיו כ"ש שם ע"ש היטב כי כל התורה שמקבלין וממשיכין משם מהרשימו של הביטול הנ"ל צריכין להמשיכה ע"י תפילה ותחנונים וכמבואר בדבריו ז"ל בכמה מקומות בהתור' ראיתי והנה מנורת זהב סי' ח'. ע"פ ומעין מבית ה'יצא ובהתו' ט' תקונין וכו'. וכן מובן בהתו' הזאת שמתחיל לדבר לעשות אחד מכל התפילה ע"י ההסתכלות על התכלית. ואח"כ מסיים שע"י ההסתכלות על התכלית ממשיכן תורה מהרשימו ע"ש. אך באמת הכל אחד כי תורה ותפילה תלויים זה בזה כי הארת הזריחת הרשימו הקדושה והנוראה הנ"ל שנשארת מהביטול צריכין תחילה להמשיכה על עצמו ולקשרה בגופו היטב ע"י תפילה שהיא בח'י שורש ומקור המעין הנמשך מהרשימו הנ"ל. ואח"כ מתפשט המעין ונעשה מזה חידושי תורה ועי"ז מקרר ומבטל היסורין. כי ע"יהתפילה והתורה נעשים כלים שעי"ז יכולין לקבל שפע חסדו לטובה לחיים נצחיים ולא לרעה ולמות מיתת עולם ח"ו עי"ז וכנ"ל וע"כ באמת אין אדם יודע איך להתפלל כ"א צדקי אדור האמתיים וכשרז"ל מי שיש לו חולה בתוך ביתו ילך אצל חכם כי א"א להביא אל התכלית כ"א הצדיק האמתי שהוא בבחי' בעל השדה הנאמר שם בתחלית התורה הנ"ל שהוא מסתכל על כל מי שרחוק עדיין מהתכלית ואין תפילתו כלולה באחד שיראה להביאו אל התכלית שתהי' תפילתו כלול באחד ע"ש. וע"כ שלמה בעת שהתפלל כשנגמר הביהמ"ק שישמע הש"י תפילת ישראל המכוונים דעתם לשם אמר בפירוש ונתת לאיש ככל דרכיו אשרתדעאת לבבו וכו' וכשפרש"י שם אם אתה יודע שהוא משחית בממונו את חבירו אל תתן לו ע"ש. וע"כ באמת יש בזה נפלאות תמים דעים ואין מי שיודע להתפלל כראוי כ"א צדיקים האמתיים כנ"ל ושאר בני עולם צריכין לקשר תפילתם להצדיקים הנ"ל והם יעלו תפילתם כראוי שימשיכו להם שפע מה שצריכין בני חיי ומזוני וכו' באופן שלא יזיק להם לנצח ח"ו רק אדרבא ע"י השפע דייקא יתתקנו וישווב אל ה' וזה שדקדק שם שלמה בתפילתו כיאתה ידעת לבדך את לבב כל בני האדם למען ייראוך כל הימים וכו' היינו שביקש שימלא הש"י תפילת ישראל מה שמבקשים אבל יהי' רק לטובה שיזכו ליראה מלפניו ית' עי"ז וכנ"ל. רק על הנכרי התפלל ועשית ככל אשר יקרא אליך הנכרי וכו' ופרש" ישם כדי שלא יקרא תגר וכו' ובשביל זה מתפללין לפעמים הצדיקים על הרשעים והרחוקים הבאים אליהם שיהי' להם עשירות והכל בשביל קדושת השם כדי שלא יקראו תגר ויקלקל להם יותר וע"כ באמת יש בענין זה של התפילה נפלאות ונסתרות הרבה וע"כ באמת אסור להתעקש ולדחוק עצמו על שום דבר בתפילתו רק אם יתן הש"י יתן ואם לאו לאו כ"ש בהתו' ט' תקונין. כי אולי א"א למלאות בקשתו אפי' ע"י התפלה כי יזיק לו יותר ח"ו כשימלאו בקשתו וכנ"ל ואם ידחוק ויתעקש בתפילתו יכול להיות שיטריח את הש"י עד שימלא בקשתו כי בשביל זה ברא את האדם שיהי' כח בתפילתו להמשיך כל ההשפעות כנ"ל. אבל לא יהי' לו לטובה כי אין כח בתפילתו לתקן הכלי שצריך לקבלת השפע שוא רוצה:
aligned_segments.en: This halacha is one of the most architecturally magnificent in all of Likutay Halachos. Reb Nosson weaves together a single unifying thread through a breathtaking range of topics: eating, faith, intellect, speech, exile and redemption, Pesach, the Counting of the Omer, the Temple service, and melichah (salting meat). At its core is the teaching from Likutay Moharan 1:62, which is amplified and applied across halacha, history, and practical daily life.
